harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (Alpine 3.23), built a local apk package repository from packages fetched to local storage (musl, tree), served it via a persistent darkhttpd OpenRC service on $NODE_IP:8080 backed by /var/www/localhost/htdocs/localrepo. Simulated the usual remote repositories (dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org) being unreachable via a hosts-file DNS sinkhole, proved the remote was unreachable with curl (connection refused), then installed the `tree` package purely from the local HTTP repo while remote repos returned connection-refused errors. Verified the package is genuinely functional (tree v2.2.1 binary runs). Cleaned up the DNS sinkhole afterward to restore normal connectivity, leaving the local repo (with remote fallback) permanently configured. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health, issued a background `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnection, polled node1 until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed (82a04a58... -> a0d41fb7...) and boot time reset, and verified post-restart that the darkhttpd service auto-started, the local repo is served, tree remains installed, and apk update still shows the local repo reachable and remote repos unreachable-but-listed (real internet access was restored, confirmed working, before restart).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline OS/apk/boot state
Fetched tree + musl packages from remote repo into a local directory while remote was still reachable
Built APKINDEX.tar.gz with apk index
Installed darkhttpd from remote repo before cutting off remote access
Served the local repo directory via darkhttpd on $NODE_IP:8080, verified with curl
Added local repo to /etc/apk/repositories (placed first for priority)
Sinkholed dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org in /etc/hosts to 127.0.0.1
Proved remote unreachability via curl connection-refused and apk update WARNINGs
Installed tree via apk add --allow-untrusted, sourced entirely from the local repo, verified binary functionality
Moved repo content under /var/www/localhost/htdocs/localrepo, configured /etc/conf.d/darkhttpd, enabled darkhttpd via rc-update/rc-service for boot persistence
Restored /etc/hosts to remove the sinkhole and confirmed remote connectivity returned
Captured pre-restart boot_id, uptime, service status, repo reachability, and installed-package proof
Triggered a backgrounded `reboot` on node1 so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 exec availability until it recovered
Confirmed new boot_id and reset uptime as proof of an actual restart

Verified post-restart recovery: darkhttpd auto-started, local repo reachable, tree still installed and functional, /etc/hosts clean, apk update reflects local-reachable/remote-unreachable-if-tested state
Cleaned up temporary files and backups

evidence.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
evidence.summary: Packages fetched locally, indexed with apk index, served via darkhttpd (first as a foreground test process, then as a persistent OpenRC service) with curl confirming APKINDEX.tar.gz is reachable over HTTP from local storage.

DNS sinkhole for dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org caused curl to fail with 'Connection refused', and apk update showed WARNING: Connection refused for both remote main/community repos while the local repo responded.

evidence.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while remote is unreachable
evidence.summary: apk add --allow-untrusted tree succeeded (exit=0) sourcing only from the local repo (remote still showing connection-refused in the same apk update output); apk info -e tree and `tree --version` confirm real, functional installation.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (82a04a58-92bb-4007-ba72-ce108f861a2f), darkhttpd service status 'started', and confirmed tree installed/functional immediately before initiating restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `sleep 2; reboot` returned an immediate acknowledgement (PID) to the exec call before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection reset/timeout) during reboot, then exec succeeded again with a new boot_id (a0d41fb7-ae61-457b-822d-2a614884a8ba) and reset boot time (2026-09-04 23:03:51), proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: After restart, darkhttpd service auto-started and is listening on 8080, the local repo index is fetchable again, tree remains installed and functional, and apk update again shows the local repo active — confirming full recovery.
